# https://refinzi.com/ llms-full.txt

# Refinzi — Browser-Native AI Prompt Layer & Autonomous Calibration Engine

> Last updated: 2026 | Version: 2.1.0 | License: MIT (Open Source)
> Canonical URL: https://refinzi.com/
> Companion files: https://refinzi.com/llms.txt (summary), https://refinzi.com/sitemap.xml

---

## Executive Overview & Value Proposition

Refinzi is a free, open-source browser extension (Manifest V3 WebExtension) that rewrites rough,
natural-language drafts into high-quality AI prompts **in-place**, directly inside the composer of
the AI tool the user is already using. It is best described as **"Grammarly for prompts."**

The user writes the way they think. Refinzi reads the draft, infers intent, and replaces the text
with a calibrated prompt the AI can execute far better. There is no separate window, no
questionnaire, and no mandatory follow-up questions.

Refinzi is not a prompt *library* and not a chatbot. It is an ambient interaction layer that docks a
small Orb beside the active composer. The entire product surface is one physical control with two
behaviours:

* **Click the Orb (< 350 ms) → ⚡ Better Prompt.** An instant, single-pass refiner that preserves the
  user's own voice and objective while adding structure, deliverables, constraints and quality
  criteria.
* **Press and hold the Orb (≥ 350 ms) → 🧠 Expert Prompt.** A deeper, autonomous calibration pass that
  performs task reconstruction (*Understand → Infer → Assume → Execute*) and emits a
  senior-practitioner-grade briefing with defensible assumptions.

In both modes the result is written straight back into the AI composer, with a floating
`[↩ Undo]` toast so the original draft is never lost. The user then presses Enter/Send in their AI
tool as normal.

**Why it matters:** most users know *what* they want but not *how* to instruct a model. Refinzi
removes that translation burden without forcing them to learn prompt engineering or answer forms.

---

## Core Metrics & Technical Specifications

| Attribute | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Product Type** | Cross-browser WebExtension (Manifest V3) |
| **Supported Browsers** | Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox |
| **Supported AI Sites** | ChatGPT (chatgpt.com), Claude (claude.ai), Google Gemini (gemini.google.com), Perplexity (perplexity.ai) |
| **Generic Fallback** | Any web page containing a `textarea` or `contenteditable` element |
| **Primary Interface** | Ambient in-composer Orb (draggable; double-click resets position) |
| **Interaction Model** | Click = Better Prompt; Hold ≥ 350 ms = Expert Prompt |
| **Hold Threshold** | 350 ms (user-adjustable 300–600 ms in Settings) |
| **Output Behaviour** | Automatic in-place replacement with floating `[↩ Undo]` toast |
| **Default Engine** | Built-in deterministic synthesis engine — on-device, zero API keys, no network call |
| **Optional Engines** | Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK): OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter |
| **Prompt Storage** | None server-side. Optional local history in `chrome.storage.local`, one-click clearable |
| **Content Telemetry** | None |
| **Questions Asked** | Zero in both modes |
| **Distribution** | `refinzi-chrome-v2.1.0.zip`, `refinzi-edge-v2.1.0.zip`, `refinzi-firefox-v2.1.0.zip` |
| **Repository** | https://github.com/papada1472/refinzi |
| **Test Suite** | 87 automated unit & integration tests (Vitest) |

---

## Interaction Model: The Single Unified Control

Refinzi deliberately exposes **one** control instead of a menu of tools. This is the core design
decision of the product.

1. **Ambient docking.** A content script uses mutation observers and SPA navigation handlers to
   detect the active composer on supported sites, then docks the Orb beside it. No brittle
   selectors; adapters degrade to a generic fallback.
2. **Click detection.** A pointer-down followed by pointer-up inside the 350 ms window is treated as
   a click → Better mode.
3. **Hold detection.** Exceeding 350 ms triggers Expert mode immediately, with a visual progress
   indicator on the Orb so the user understands the mode switch in real time.
4. **Drag vs. click disambiguation.** Movement greater than 6 px is treated as a drag (repositioning)
   and never triggers refinement. Double-clicking the Orb resets it to the default dock position.
5. **In-place injection.** The calibrated prompt is written back into the composer using
   framework-aware strategies: ProseMirror caret-range insertion, `execCommand` with synthetic
   selection, native value descriptor setters, and input/change event dispatch. React, Quill,
   ProseMirror and Lexical controlled inputs all stay in sync.
6. **Undo.** A floating `[↩ Undo]` toast restores the exact pre-refinement draft with one click.
---

## The Four Primary Operator Archetypes

Refinzi's calibration engine detects the likely domain from the raw draft and adapts its
assumptions. Four archetypes recur most often:

### 1. Marketers, Founders & Growth Operators
Drafts like *"make a marketing plan for my b2b saas"* become structured plans with audience pain
points, acquisition angles, an execution blueprint with weekly milestones, and KPIs. Expert mode adds
positioning, unit economics, churn risk and channel-saturation analysis.

### 2. Engineers & Technical Builders
Drafts like *"fix my react state bug"* become precise technical briefs specifying stack version
constraints, reproduction conditions, the required diagnostic reasoning, and the acceptance criteria
the answer must satisfy.

### 3. Researchers, Analysts & Writers
Drafts like *"summarize this study"* become methodological briefs that ask for the study design, the
evidence standard, epistemic caveats, and a clearly labelled separation of fact from inference.

### 4. Creators & Content Producers
Drafts like *"a samurai walking through a rainy city at night"* become layered creative briefs with
subject, environment, lighting, camera specification, mood and format parameters suitable for image
and video generation tools.

---

## Primary Workflows & Interaction Mechanics

### 1. Click → Instant Better Prompt

* **Trigger:** pointer-down and release within 350 ms on the Orb.
* **Engine:** single-pass calibration.
* **What it does:** extracts the raw objective, resolves ambiguity into explicit constraints, adds the
  structural sections a strong answer needs (deliverable, format, quality bar, edge cases), and
  removes vague filler — without inflating the prompt into a 1,000-word template.
* **What it preserves:** the user's original intent, terminology, named tools and framing.
* **Latency:** instant when using the built-in local engine.

### 2. Hold → Autonomous Expert Briefing

* **Trigger:** pointer held on the Orb for 350 ms or longer.
* **Engine:** multi-pass task reconstruction.
* **Pipeline:** *Understand → Infer → Assume → Execute.*
  1. **Understand** — classify the task type, domain and implicit deliverable.
  2. **Infer** — determine the expert role the answer requires, plus the audience and success metric
     the user did not state.
  3. **Assume** — commit to specific, defensible values for everything still unknown (sector, scale,
     budget band, tone, constraints) and state those assumptions explicitly inside the prompt.
  4. **Execute** — emit a structured briefing: Role & Perspective, Core Objective, Calibrated
     Parameters, Methodology & Quality Requirements, Required Deliverable.
* **Critical behaviour:** Expert mode **never asks the user a question.** It resolves uncertainty by
  making assumptions and declaring them, so the interaction never stalls.

### 3. Send to the AI normally

After refinement the prompt sits in the composer exactly as if the user had typed it. No copy-paste,
no second window, no context switch. The user presses Enter in their own AI tool.

## Real-World Before & After Demonstrations

### Scenario A: Marketing & Growth Strategy

**Raw input:** *"make a marketing plan for my b2b saas"*

**⚡ Better Prompt output:**

> Create a high-converting, practical 90-day marketing plan for a B2B SaaS.
>
> Include:
> 1. Target audience pain points — the emotional triggers that make them act now.
> 2. Three distinct acquisition angles: counterintuitive, direct benefit, and story-driven.
> 3. A ready-to-use execution blueprint with weekly milestones.
> 4. Actionable KPIs for pipeline and free-trial conversion.
>
> Tone: punchy, direct, zero corporate fluff.

**🧠 Expert Prompt output:**

> Act as a World-Class Growth Strategist.
>
> Objective: Build a 90-day marketing plan for a B2B SaaS targeting founders and execs, with a goal
> of driving direct free-trial signups.
>
> Methodology: Break down unit economics and acquisition loops step-by-step, address churn risk and
> channel saturation, and state all growth benchmarks and conversion-rate assumptions upfront.
>
> Deliverable: A phased 90-day implementation matrix with clear weekly checkpoints and conversion
> metrics.
>
> Tone: production-grade, high-leverage, zero fluff.

### Scenario B: Production Coding

**Raw input:** *"fix my react state bug"*

**⚡ Better Prompt output:**

> Diagnose and fix the React state bug in my component.
>
> Include:
> 1. The most likely root cause, ranked by probability.
> 2. The exact minimal code change required.
> 3. Why the bug occurs (stale closure, mutation, batching, or effect timing).
> 4. How to verify the fix and prevent regression.
>
> Output a single corrected code block with inline comments explaining each change.

**🧠 Expert Prompt output:**

> Act as a Senior React Engineer specialising in state management and render performance.
>
> Objective: Diagnose and resolve a state-synchronisation defect in a React component and harden it
> against recurrence.
>
> Methodology: Reason from React's batching and effect-timing semantics. Enumerate the competing
> hypotheses (stale closure, direct state mutation, dependency-array omission, derived-state drift),
> eliminate each against the symptom, and justify the surviving root cause.
>
> Deliverable: A minimal, production-safe patch, plus a regression test that fails before the fix and
> passes after it.
>
> Assumptions: Function components with hooks; React 18+ concurrent rendering enabled.
>
> Quality bar: No speculative rewrites, no dependency upgrades unless strictly required.

### Scenario C: Deep Research & Analysis

**Raw input:** *"summarize this study"*

**🧠 Expert Prompt output:**

> Act as a Research Analyst with expertise in study design and evidence appraisal.
>
> Objective: Produce a rigorous, decision-ready summary of the supplied study.
>
> Methodology: Separate the study's stated claims from its demonstrated evidence. Assess design
> validity, sample adequacy, confounding risk, and statistical significance. Distinguish correlation
> from causation and flag every place where the data does not support the headline conclusion.
>
> Deliverable: A structured summary covering design, population, intervention, measured outcomes,
> effect sizes with confidence intervals, stated limitations, and a clearly labelled "what this does
> not establish" section.
>
> Assumptions: Peer-reviewed source; single study rather than a meta-analysis.
>
> Quality bar: No inference presented as fact. Any uncertainty is explicitly marked.

## Detailed Architectural Comparison: Refinzi vs. The Landscape

| Dimension | Refinzi | Prompt library sites | Copy-paste prompt templates | AI-native chat add-ons |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Operating System** | Any (browser extension) | Any (web) | Any (web) | Any (web) |
| **Where it works** | In-place inside the AI composer | Separate website | Separate website | Inside one specific AI product |
| **Interaction cost** | One click, or one hold | Search, copy, paste | Copy, paste, edit | Open panel, follow form |
| **Questions asked** | Zero | N/A | N/A | Often many |
| **Prompt preservation** | Automatic in-place + 1-click Undo | Manual | Manual | Manual |
| **Expert-mode reasoning** | Autonomous inference with stated assumptions | None | None | Rare |
| **Default engine** | On-device, zero API key | N/A | N/A | Vendor-hosted |
| **Prompt storage** | None server-side | Account-linked | None | Account-linked |
| **Cost** | Free & open source (MIT) | Often freemium/subscription | Free | Bundled subscription |

**Key differentiator:** Refinzi is not a destination. It is a layer that meets the user inside the tool
they already have open, and it resolves ambiguity autonomously rather than by interrogation.

---

## Security, Privacy & Local-First Architecture

### 1. Zero Prompt Storage

User prompts are never transmitted to, logged by, or retained on any Refinzi-operated server. In the
default configuration the synthesis engine runs entirely on-device and the prompt never leaves the
browser tab.

### 2. No Content Telemetry

No prompt text, generated output, or conversation content is collected for analytics. Refinzi does
not train on user data.

### 3. Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) Isolation

When a user optionally configures a provider key, all network calls are issued from the extension's
**background service worker**, never from the page context. Web pages cannot observe raw credentials,
and keys are stored in the extension's own isolated storage area.

### 4. Minimal Permission Surface

The extension requests host permissions only for the four supported AI sites, plus a generic
`activeTab`-style fallback for arbitrary textareas. It is declarative in Manifest V3 with no remote
code execution.

### 5. Verifiable & Auditable

Refinzi is MIT-licensed and fully open source. Every build artefact can be reproduced locally from the
repository using the documented build script, and no minified third-party bundle is injected into
pages.

### 6. Local History Control

Optional transformation history is stored only in the browser's local extension storage on the user's
own machine, is never synced to a server, and can be cleared at any time with one click in Settings.
Optional transformation history is stored only in the browser's local extension storage on the user's
own machine, is never synced to a server, and can be cleared at any time with one click in Settings.

---

## Supported AI Models & Routing Architecture

Refinzi is model-agnostic. It refines the *instruction*, not the answer, so it works with whatever
model the user has open in their AI tool. Two routing paths exist:

### 1. Built-in Local Engine (Default)

* Deterministic, template-free synthesis running on-device.
* Requires no API key and no account.
* Produces Better and Expert prompts instantly with zero network latency.
* Prompt text never leaves the browser tab.

### 2. Bring-Your-Own-Key (Optional)

Any of the following providers can be configured in extension Settings for higher-ceiling Expert
briefings. All requests originate from the background service worker over direct HTTPS with no
intermediary:

* **OpenAI** — GPT-class models
* **Anthropic** — Claude models
* **Google Gemini** — Gemini models
* **DeepSeek** — DeepSeek models
* **OpenRouter** — any routed open-weight model

The user chooses the provider and model. Refinzi applies no markup and imposes no quota.

---

## The Calibration Engine Specification

Both modes share one semantic spine and diverge only in depth.

**Shared semantic spine (both modes):**

1. **Objective extraction** — isolate what the user actually wants produced.
2. **Domain classification** — marketing, engineering, research, creative, business, general.
3. **Missing-dimension analysis** — identify which of the dimensions that determine output quality are
   absent from the draft.
4. **Cliché suppression** — strip generic filler phrases and replace them with concrete requirements.
5. **Deliverable specification** — state the exact artefact the model must return.

**Better Prompt (Click) — added layer:**

* Structures the draft into explicit deliverable, format and quality criteria.
* Keeps length proportionate; explicitly avoids 1,000-word boilerplate.
* Preserves the user's own voice, named tools and terminology.

**Expert Prompt (Hold) — added layers:**

* **Role & Perspective** — assigns the expert identity the answer requires.
* **Calibrated Parameters** — locks in audience, format, tone, scope and constraints.
* **Methodology & Quality Requirements** — instructs how to reason: step-by-step derivation,
  uncertainty handling, edge-case coverage, and separation of fact from inference.
* **Assumption Declaration** — every inferred value is stated inside the prompt so the model's output
  is auditable rather than silently biased.
* **Required Deliverable** — a precise specification including structure, checkpoints and metrics.

**What neither mode ever does:**

* Ask the user a clarifying question.
* Open a form, wizard, or questionnaire.
* Require a file upload.
* Emit a generic marketing or coding template unrelated to the draft.
* Send the prompt to a Refinzi server.

## Pricing & Licensing

### Free & Open Source — $0, Forever

* Full Better mode (Click) completely free.
* Full Expert mode (Hold) completely free.
* Built-in on-device engine with zero API keys required.
* Unlimited use on Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
* Optional BYOK with zero markup if the user supplies their own provider key.
* No account, no sign-up, no trial expiry, no feature paywall.

### License

MIT License. The source is fully available at https://github.com/papada1472/refinzi and may be
inspected, forked, self-built and redistributed under the terms of the license.

### No Subscription

There is no recurring subscription, no per-token billing operated by Refinzi, and no in-extension
payment flow. Any provider charges the user may incur come directly from the third-party API provider
they choose to configure themselves.

## Installation, Verification & Building from Source

### 1. Install from a Release Package

Production packages are published at https://refinzi.com/downloads/ and in the repository releases:

* `refinzi-chrome-v2.1.0.zip` — Google Chrome
* `refinzi-edge-v2.1.0.zip` — Microsoft Edge
* `refinzi-firefox-v2.1.0.zip` — Mozilla Firefox

**Chrome / Edge:**

1. Open `chrome://extensions/` (or `edge://extensions/`).
2. Enable **Developer mode** in the top-right corner.
3. Click **Load unpacked** and select the unzipped package directory.
4. Open ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity — the Refinzi Orb appears beside the composer.

**Firefox:**

1. Open `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox`.
2. Choose **Load Temporary Add-on** and select the package's `manifest.json`.

### 2. Build from Source

```bash
# 1. Clone the official repository
git clone https://github.com/papada1472/refinzi.git

# 2. Navigate to the project root
cd refinzi

# 3. Install dependencies
npm install

# 4. Run the automated test suite (87 tests)
npx vitest run

# 5. Type-check the extension source
npm run typecheck

# 6. Build all browser targets and produce the release zips
npm run build
```

The build writes per-browser bundles to `dist/chrome/`, `dist/edge/` and `dist/firefox/`, and
release archives into `landing/public/downloads/`.

### 3. Verifying a Build

* Every generated package contains a `manifest.json` declaring `manifest_version: 3`.
* No remote scripts are referenced; all logic ships inside the archive.
* SHA256 checksums are published alongside each release for independent verification.
> Quality bar: No speculative rewrites, no dependency upgrades unless strictly required.
